_meta.description: The five events this site defines for click and conversion measurement (brief: 'record the five defined events'). This file defines them; it does not contain measurements. Every count row is null because no authorised first-party report has been obtained - a count can only enter this file from an Associates Central report or from the site's own opted-in endpoint, never from an estimate.
_meta.privacy_rule: No cookie, no fingerprint, no session replay, no cross-site identifier and no personal data. The client-side record holds the event name, the page path, the product ASIN and the browser's own timestamp, in localStorage, on the visitor's machine. Nothing is transmitted: the endpoint pair below is deliberately null.
_meta.opt_in_rule: Transmission is off until the reader opts in on the analytics page, and both endpoint fields are empty by default. With endpoint_step1 and endpoint_step2 both null the outbound-click counter still records locally and never calls the network - the fetch is guarded by a null check, so an unconfigured endpoint cannot leak a request.
_meta.endpoint_note: A self-hosted collector is two steps this repository cannot take on the owner's behalf: (1) deploy a small server that accepts a POST and stores one row per event; (2) put its URL in endpoint_step1 and the collector's public documentation URL in endpoint_step2. Until both exist the site does not guess a hostname: a wrong endpoint would either drop data silently or send a reader's events to a third party, which is what the privacy rule above rules out.
_meta.source_of_truth: Authoritative click, order and commission figures come only from Associates Central reporting. This file records the on-site half of the funnel (impression, outbound click) that Amazon cannot see.

events.name: product_impression
events.fired_when: A product card or a product table row is at least half visible in the viewport for one second (IntersectionObserver; no scroll handler). Fires once per product per page view.
events.why: Answers 'was the product seen at all'. Without it, a page with no clicks cannot be told apart from a page nobody scrolled to.
events.personal_data: None. The page path and the ASIN are public. The timestamp is the browser clock at the moment of view.
events.stored_in: localStorage key zone4.events.v1 on the visitor's device.
events.transmitted: No, unless the reader opts in and an endpoint is configured.

events.name: product_cta_click
events.fired_when: The reader activates a call-to-action control that is not itself the outbound link - for example the 'Read the full review' button on a product card.
events.why: Separates interest from departure. A reader who opens the review and a reader who leaves for the shop are different outcomes, and only this event makes the difference visible.
events.transmitted: No, unless the reader opts in and an endpoint is configured.

events.name: affiliate_click
events.fired_when: The browser follows an outbound Amazon link carrying rel="sponsored". The event is written to local storage before the navigation starts.
events.why: The denominator for every later conversion claim, and the one number on this site that is both first-party and honestly obtainable.
events.personal_data: None. destination_host records the Amazon host the reader was sent to, so a mis-set link is visible in the log.
events.transmitted: No, unless the reader opts in and an endpoint is configured.

events.name: guide_read_complete
events.fired_when: The reader reaches the end of an article body: the last paragraph of the review or guide passes half the viewport. Fires once per article per page view.
events.why: Tells an editorial session which guides are actually read rather than merely opened - the question a publishing cadence has to answer before a second wave is written.
events.transmitted: No, unless the reader opts in and an endpoint is configured.

events.name: disclosure_viewed
events.fired_when: The disclosure strip under the masthead has been in the viewport for one second on the current page. Fires once per page view.
events.why: A compliance check, not a marketing one: it evidences that the required sentence was actually shown above the fold, which is what the FTC and the Operating Agreement ask for and what no click count can show.
events.transmitted: No, unless the reader opts in and an endpoint is configured.

unknown_events.note: Funnel stages the brief names that this site cannot honestly emit. Listed as unknowns, never as zeroes.

rows.why_unknown: Happens on Amazon, after the reader leaves this site. Only Associates Central can report it.
Same as above. What counts as a qualifying purchase is defined by the Commission Income Statement, not by anything this site can observe.
